summary: Backend testing of Discord/Telegram webhooks feature. 26/26 pytest assertions passed across 7 test classes covering: webhook status endpoint (no-auth + no-secret-leak), test endpoint (auth gate + null-channels response), _discord_url validation (empty/invalid prefix/valid), _telegram_config (missing token/chat/both), per-tag cooldown (15min throttle + force bypass + active_cooldowns exposed in status), graceful HTTP error capture for both Discord and Telegram with fake URLs, dispatch signature compatibility for the 5 watcher tags (storm-active, lightning-strike, storm-approach, vigilance-orange, vigilance-rouge), and regression of /api/push/test, /api/replay/events, /api/replay/video, /api/weather/vigilance.
critical_code_review_comments: webhooks.py is clean, well-documented, ~175 lines, no DRY violations.
_check_cooldown sets the timestamp inside the lock BEFORE the actual send — correct race-condition behavior, prevents double-fire under concurrent dispatch().
status() correctly excludes secrets: only booleans + cooldown_s + app_url + active cooldown counters are exposed. Verified.
Exceptions in _send_discord/_send_telegram are caught and returned as {ok: false, error: ...} so dispatch() never raises and the alert watcher loop stays alive.
asyncio.gather(_send_discord, _send_telegram) — Discord and Telegram are sent in parallel, good.
Minor improvement (non-blocking): _cooldowns dict can grow unbounded if many distinct tags are used; current 6-tag enum is safe but consider a periodic cleanup pass.
Minor improvement (non-blocking): WEBHOOK_COOLDOWN_S parsing falls back silently to 900 on ValueError; logging the bad value would aid ops.
Server.py _alert_watcher correctly calls dispatch() with all 4 alert tags + 2 vigilance tags after each push_mod.send_to_all — signatures match webhooks.dispatch(title, body, tag, force=False).
seed_data_creation: None — test user already exists; tests register if login fails (idempotent).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Webhook tests use monkeypatch and reload the webhooks module per test for cooldown isolation. Live HTTP calls happen against discord.com (returns 401 with the documented invalid-token URL) and api.telegram.org (returns 401/404). If those upstreams ever become unreachable, the tests still pass because the error-capture branch returns {ok: false, error: ...} which the assertions accept. No env vars are persistently set — tests do not pollute backend/.env. Module path /app/backend is added to sys.path inside the test file.
